Short title and commencement

THE MERCHANT SHIPPING (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1966
THE MERCHANT SHIPPING (AMENDMENT) ORDIN ANCE, 1966
ORDINANCE No. VI of 1966
(Approved by the National Assembly of
Pakistan on the 31st May, 1966, see Gaz. of P., 1966, Ext., pp. 336-344 (R).)
[21st May, 1966]
An Ordinance further to amend the Merchant Shipping Act, 1923
WHEREAS an International
Convention for promoting safety of life at sea was signed in London on the
seventeenth day of June, 1960, replacing the International Convention for the
Safety of Life at Sea signed in London on the tenth day of June, 1948, which
was given effect to by Pakistan from the first day of May, 1955 ;
AND WHEREAS Pakistan was a
signatory to the said Inter national Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea
signed in Lon don on the seventeenth day of June, 1960 ;
AND WHEREAS in order to give
effect to the said Conven tion it is expedient further to amend the Merchant
Shipping Act, 1923, for the purposes hereinafter appearing, XXI of 1923 ;
AND WHEREAS the National Assembly
is not in session and the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which
render immediate legislation necessary ;
Now, THEREFORE, in exercise of
the powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 29 of the Constitution, and of
all other powers enabling him in that behalf, the President is pleased to make
and promulgate the following Ordinance :-
1. Short title and commencement. -(1) This Ordinance may be called
the Merchant Ship ping (Amendment) Ordinance, 1966.
(2) This section shall come into
force at once, and the rest of this Ordinance or any section thereof shall come
into force on such date or dates as the Central Government may, by notification
in the official Gazette, appoint in this behalf.

5. Amendment of section 242 Act, XXI of 1923. In the said Act, in
section 242,-
(1) for the marginal heading the
following shall be substituted, namely :-
"Requirements of
radio-telegraph and radio telephone apparatus." ; and
(2) for sub-section (1) the
following shall be substituted, namely :-
"(1) Every sea-going
Pakistan ship, being a passenger steamer of whatever tonnage, and every other
Pakistan ship of sixteen hundred tons gross tonnage or upwards shall be
provided with a radio-telegraph apparatus, and every Pakistan ship of three
hundred tons gross tonnage or upwards but under sixteen hundred tons shall be
provided with either a radio-telegraph apparatus or a radio-telephone
apparatus:
Provided that the Central
Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, exempt from the
operation of this section any ship or class of ships, if it is of the opinion
that having regard to the nature of the voyages on which the ship or ships are
engaged, or other circum stances of the case, the provision of a radio telegraph
apparatus or a radio-telephone apparatus, as the case may be, is unnecessary or
unreasonable."

6. Insertion of new section 242A, Act, XXI of 1923. In the said
Act, after section 242, the following new section shall be inserted, namely:-
"242A. Provision of radio
direction finding apparatus-
(1) Every Pakistan ship of
sixteen hundred tons gross tonnage and upwards shall be provided with a radio
direction-finding apparatus:
Provided that the Central
Government may exempt from the operation of this section any ship of less than
five thousand tons gross tonnage, not being a passenger steamer, if it is of
the opinion that, having regard to the nature of the voyages on which the ship
is engaged, the provision of radio direction finding apparatus is unnecessary
or unreasonable.
(2) If sub-section (1) is not
complied with in the case of any such ship, the master or owner of the ship
shall be liable in respect of each offence to a fine which may extend to one
thousand rupees."

10. Insertion of new sections 145B and 245BB, Act XXI of 1923. In
the said Act, after section 245AA and before the heading "Safety
Convention Certificates", the following heading and new sections shall be
inserted, namely :-
"Additional Requirement for cargo ships
245B. Requirement of construction and survey of cargo ships.-(1)
Every sea-going Pakistan ship of not less than five hundred tons gross tonnage,
or of such lower tonnage as the Cen tral Government may, by notification in the
official Gazette, specify in this behalf, other than a passenger steamer or a
troopship, shall be constructed in accordance with such speci fications and
surveyed to such extent, in such manner and at such intervals as may he pre scribed.
(2) The provisions of this
section shall apply, in the same manner as they apply to a Pakistan ship, to
every other ship of not less than five hundred tons gross tonnage while she is
within any port in Pakistan unless there is produced in respect of such ship-
(a) a valid Safety Convention
Certificates equiva lent to a Cargo Ship Safety Construction Certificate ; or
(b) valid Safety Convention
Certificates equiva lent respectively to a Qualified Cargo Ship Safety
Construction Certificate and to a corresponding Exemption certificate.
(3) This section does not apply
to vessels to which the provisions of ills Inland Mechanically Pro pelled
Vessels Act (O of 1917), apply so long as such vessels are employed within
inland waters or are engaged in coastal shipping confined to ports within one
Province.
245BB. Power of Government to make rules with respect to the
construction and survey of cargo ships, etc.-(1) The Central Government may
make rules prescribing the requirements for the hull, equipment and machinery
of ships to which section 245B applies and the requirements of survey thereof.
(2) In particular and without
prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power, such rules may provide for
all or any of the following matters, namely :-
(a) the extent of surveys and the
manner in which and the intervals at which surveys are to be made ;
(b) the requirements as to
construction, mach inery and equipment ;
(c) the form and manner in which
declarations of surveys are to be issued and transmitted and the particulars
which are to be stated therein ;
(d) the charging of fees for
making surveys under the rules ; and
(e) such other matters as may be
necessary for carrying out the purposes of section 245B.
(3) In making a rule under this
section, the Central Government may direct that a breach of it shall be
punishable wit
sections.punishment:
punishable with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, and, when the
breach is a continuing breach, with a further fine which may extend to fifty
rupees for every day after the first during which the breach continues.

Central Government or such person as it may authorise for the purpose is

registered in Pakistan to which section 245B applies, that the steam-ship

cause to be issued in respect of the steamship-
(a) if the steam-ship is of not

from or to any place in Pakistan to or from any place outside Pakistan, a
certificate to be called a Cargo Ship Safety Construction Certificate, and in
any other case, a certificate showing that she complies with the said rules ;
or (b) if the steam-ship is partially exempt from the requirements of the
Safety Convention as to hull, equipment or machinery, a certificate to be
called a Qualified Cargo Ship Safety Con struction Certificate.
